model_annotation: Figure 10, titled “The effect of context masking on case tasks grouped by language family,” presents a bar chart illustrating the impact of context masking across different language families, with error bars indicating the standard deviation for each group. The horizontal axis lists language families—Uralic, Altaic, Indo-European, and others—while the vertical axis represents the magnitude of the effect, scaled from 0 to approximately 0.6, with tick marks at intervals of 0.1. Each bar corresponds to a language family and is color-coded: Uralic is shown in red, Altaic in green, Indo-European in blue, and the “Other” category in purple. The bar for Uralic is the tallest, reaching approximately 0.55, indicating the strongest effect of context masking on case tasks within this family. The Altaic bar is slightly shorter, around 0.45, followed by Indo-European at about 0.35, and “Other” at roughly 0.25. Error bars extend above and below each bar, with the Uralic family showing the largest standard deviation, suggesting greater variability in the effect across its constituent languages. The chart visually emphasizes that context masking has a more pronounced effect on case tasks in agglutinative language families like Uralic and Altaic compared to more analytic or fusional families.
